default allow = false

## Why This Is Asked

This question probes practical design for per-tenant feature gating in CNF gateways, including secure identity, dynamic policy delivery, and runtime enforcement. It emphasizes end-to-end testability and real-world trade-offs between performance and isolation.

## Key Concepts

- per-tenant policy CRD
- bidirectional gRPC capability negotiation
- in-memory enforcement with cache invalidation
- SPIFFE/SVID-based mutual TLS for control plane–sidecar trust
- canary-friendly rollout and end-to-end validation

## Code Example

```yaml
# Minimal CRD blueprint (high level)
apiVersion: apiextensions.k8s.io/v1
kind: CustomResourceDefinition
metadata:
  name: cnffeaturepolicies.example.com
spec:
  group: example.com
  versions:
    - name: v1
      served: true
      storage: true
      schema:
        openAPIV3Schema:
          type: object
          properties:
            spec:
              type: object
              properties:
                tenantID:
                  type: string
                features:
                  type: array
                  items:
                    type: string
  scope: Namespaced
  names:
    plural: cnffeaturepolicies
    singular: cnffeaturepolicy
    kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
    shortNames: [cfp]
```

```yaml
# Sample policy (per-tenant)
apiVersion: example.com/v1
kind: CNFFeaturePolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-a-policy
spec:
  tenantID: tenant-a
  features:
    - QUIC
    - TLS13
    - multiplexing
```

```yaml
# Minimal end-to-end test manifest (one namespace)
apiVersion: v1
kind: Namespace
metadata:
  name: tenant-a
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: gateway
  namespace: tenant-a
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: gateway
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: gateway
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: gateway
          image: mycnf/gateway:latest
          args: ["--config", "/etc/gateway/config.yaml"]
          volumeMounts:
            - name: config
              mountPath: /etc/gateway

          configMap:
            name: gateway-config
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design a compliant telemetry stack for CNF gateways with multi-tenant segregation and data privacy.

## Key Concepts
- Telemetry pipelines (OpenTelemetry, Fluent Bit) across logs and traces
- Tenant context propagation and isolation
- PII masking via in-line filters (e.g., Lua) before forwarding
- Loki/Jaeger exporters and per-tenant pipelines

## Code Example
```yaml
# Fluent Bit ConfigMap snippet (Lua filter used for masking)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: fluent-bit-pp
data:
  lua-filter.lua: |
    function filter(tag, dt)
      if dt["message"] ~= nil then
        dt["message"] = (dt["message"]):gsub("%w+@%w+%.%w+", "[REDACTED_EMAIL]")
      end
      return dt
    end
```
```yaml
# OTEL collector snippet (simplified)
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: otel-collector-config
data:
  collector.yaml: |-
    receivers:
      otlp:
        protocols:
          grpc: {}
          http: {}
    processors:
      attributes:
        actions: [insert]
        keys: [tenant_id]
        from_context: true
    exporters:
      jaeger: {}
      loki: {}
    service:
      pipelines:
        traces:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [attributes]
          exporters: [jaeger]
        logs:
          receivers: [otlp]
          processors: [attributes]
          exporters: [loki]
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test cross-tenant leakage in logs/traces?
- What metrics would verify isolation and masking effectiveness?

apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: otel-config
data:
  otel.yaml: |
    receivers:
